solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Security man often taken on board

definitions.meaning: something left as security, a pledge handed over against a loan
the lowliest chess piece, the one most often captured on the chessboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Security man' reads as a guard, but it splits into two definitions: a pledge, and the chess piece most often lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge at a pawnbroker's and the humblest chess piece share the same four-letter name.

clue.text: Listen to recording, and give pound in refund

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the other phrase

parts.note: to pay back is to refund money
L stands for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone hears a recording and is given a pound as a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L into PAYBACK after its first letter; 'and give' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To play back a tape is to run it again so it can be heard.

clue.text: With over furlong vandalised, it's criminal

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece comes first
vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A racecourse's furlong has been vandalised, which is criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' tempts a reversal, but in a down clue it means the W sits above the rest; 'vandalised' signals the anagram of FURLONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongful means unlawful, as in wrongful arrest, so it fits criminal.

clue.text: Dream is to settle in part of New York

parts.note: to dream of something is to long for it
taken as written
to settle, as a bird or plane comes down, is to land

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of settling down in a district of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The island east of Manhattan holds Brooklyn and Queens, two of the city's boroughs.

clue.text: Invigorating air round region

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: Bracing air blows round a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a loose term for fresh, bracing seaside air.

clue.text: Relative's guarded, initially, about a gibe

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is a relative

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a gibe is a taunt

explanation.surface: A relative was guarded, at first, about a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives G from guarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a family member two generations up.

clue.text: Being soppy, drove one crazy

parts.note: to drive someone mad is to send them mad
I is the Roman numeral one
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Being so sloppy, someone drove a person mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drove one crazy' reads as an idiom but splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy means mawkishly emotional, so being soppy is being overly tender-hearted.

clue.text: A taxi brought over American? You can count on it!

indicators.note: brought over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A taxi brings over an American, someone reliable to count on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns CAB into BAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads is used for counting, so it is literally counted on.

clue.text: Hesitate, tired out crossing top of hill

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters go across, round the next piece
out means not in order, so the letters are rearranged
top of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tired walker hesitates as they cross the top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes DITER from tired; 'crossing' wraps it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to waver indecisively, a synonym for hesitate.

clue.text: A cat — ounce?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking whether an ounce counts as a kind of cat.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is also the snow leopard, so the surface pretends to ask about big cats; here ounce means a tiny amount, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are by-words for the tiniest quantity: not an ounce of sense, not an atom of truth.

clue.text: Offend a tar, at sea, running along the length of the ship

definitions.text: running along the length of the ship

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor is insulted somewhere along the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the nautical picture of the tar, but it signals the anagram of OFFENDATAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical phrase describes rigging or a line laid from bow to stern, lengthwise down the vessel.

clue.text: Start to comprehend socially acceptable English dance

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the first word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to start is to begin
U is the old upper-class label for what is socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone is starting to understand a refined English dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to comprehend' looks like 'begin to understand', but 'to comprehend' is the container signal: BEGIN holds U.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean ballroom dance in bolero rhythm, made famous by Cole Porter's song.

clue.text: With it, can French actor reverse negative spell?

parts.note: with it means fashionable, in
taken as written
Jacques Tati was a French actor and director

indicators.note: reverse means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: Can a trendy French actor undo a negative spell?
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' reads as a verb for the actor, but it turns only NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation is a set of words chanted as a magic charm.

clue.text: Popular leader, one in France entering race

indicators.note: entering means the French word goes into the other piece

parts.note: a race of people is a tribe
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A popular figure, one in France, enters a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in France' looks like a location, but it is the French word for one; 'entering' sends it into the word for race.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a tribune was an official elected to champion the common people.

clue.text: Child our chums ragged close to orphanage, poor creature

indicators.note: ragged means tattered and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
close to means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A child's friends are scruffy near an orphanage, a pitiful sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' turns OURCHUMS into URCHMOUS; 'close to orphanage' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase 'poor as a church mouse' makes this creature the emblem of poverty.

clue.text: College publication — leaden, unfortunately

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A college magazine is leaden, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns LEADEN into DALENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is a college at Cambridge University; Oxford's Magdalen is spelt without the final E.

clue.text: Crack marksman still

parts.note: a crack is a snap, a sharp sound or break
a good shot is a marksman

explanation.surface: A crack marksman, an expert sniper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack marksman' reads as an expert shot; still is a noun here, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, and a quick informal one is this kind of shot.

clue.text: Miscellaneous trades, so varied

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Various trades, all very different from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of mixed kinds, a direct synonym for miscellaneous.

clue.text: Bedside tables near the most original of teddy bears

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the most original part of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, tolerate it

explanation.surface: Bedside tables beside the earliest teddy bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teddy bears' reads as one toy, but splits: T from teddy, then bears as a verb meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: These small tables sit beside a bed; the term is chiefly American.

clue.text: Hand tool chauffeur finally put in Roller?

indicators.note: put in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a roller towel is a continuous loop towel on a rail

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hand tool the chauffeur finally placed in the Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: Roller looks like slang for a Rolls-Royce, which suits the chauffeur, but it is a roller towel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand-held tool for gardening or spreading mortar.

clue.text: Underwear from shopping complex in outskirts of Skegness

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the outer letters
outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a mall is a shopping complex

explanation.surface: Buying underwear at a shopping centre on the edge of Skegness, an English seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Skegness is a seaside town in Lincolnshire, England. Its outskirts are S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is British slang for underclothes, often seen on a washing line.

clue.text: Dessert made by graduate after dance

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the previous one

parts.note: the rumba is a Latin dance
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A dessert made by a graduate after a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small sponge cake soaked in rum syrup, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Nearly phone agent over love song

indicators.note: nearly means the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: to phone is to call

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Almost phoning an agent about a love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts CALL to CAL; 'over' turns SPY into YPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian song style from Trinidad, often topical and improvised.

clue.text: Salesman cutting this French material

indicators.note: cutting means the word slices into the other piece

parts.note: ce is French for this
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman cuts this French fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts REP between C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin fabric with a crinkled surface.

clue.text: Thoroughly popular at all times? Surely not!

parts.note: doing something well means doing it thoroughly
in means fashionable, popular
ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: Is someone thoroughly popular every time? Surely not!
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of astonished disbelief at something said.

clue.text: Talk about bowler, say

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
a bowler is an example of a hat, as the 'say' signals

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowler suggests cricket, but here it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk informally is to chat, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fails to secure backer somewhere in America

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: to fail is to lose
an angel is a financial backer of a show

explanation.surface: A venture fails to find a financial backer somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fails' and 'backer' suggest a theatre flop; in theatre slang a backer is an angel, and 'to secure' wraps the failing word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian city is one place in America; the vague definition is a fair hint.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery getting most of attention

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: close attention is study, as in a brown study

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery draws most of the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims STUDY to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a small earring or ornamental button fixed through a piercing.
